undisclosed_findings.finding: capture.json uses TWO different counting conventions for pinned blocks within the same file. structure.asserted_block_sha256 is per-ASSERTION (so it repeats a hash when several fields pin the same block: Step Functions has 7 entries for 4 distinct blocks), while live_reconciliation counts DISTINCT blocks ('all 4 pinned block(s)'). Both are internally consistent and the reconciliation figure is the correct one, but a reader comparing the two fields can easily mis-read the array length as the number of pinned blocks. Not a correctness defect and not blocking; worth a naming clarification in a later slice.

test_no_aws_offer_can_reach_z0 is, in isolation, a vacuous test -- this evaluator demonstrated it passes unchanged against a classifier that can never emit Z0. This is NOT a defect because the builder shipped exactly the control that fixes it, but it is worth recording explicitly that the control is load-bearing and must never be deleted as redundant.

No new instance of the known project-level gaps was introduced. sha256_stored still attests committed bytes only and each capture says so; the flattened-capture convention is unchanged; the in-cell p/li latent parser gap is untouched because five of six profiles read no table at all and the sixth's target table has no in-cell block elements.
